messages:
jess.p: Heads-up, customer reported intermittent embedding errors + huge tail latency after a traffic spike this morning :frowning:

alex.h: can you paste the error they see?

jess.p: From their logs: `ERROR ResponseError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024` — happens ~1-2% of calls during bursts. Also notice 95th latency jumps from 120ms->900ms.

maria.t: interesting. do we know which model variant they were pinned to? 1536 looks like `open-embed-large-1536` family, 1024 would be older `open-embed-mid-1024`.

sam.k: quick guess: dynamic batching coalesced requests across two model aliases that map to different underlying dims after the alias mapping change last week. Batcher groups by model alias but not final embed_dim.

jess.p: customer said they didn't change anything client-side. they do send model=rdw-open-embed (alias) and rely on autopromotion.

infra-bot: Deploy info: alias-resolution change deployed 1723340000 by deploy-bot; batcher service restarted 1723351000. Current batcher config: `max_batch_size=64`, `dynamic_batching=true`, `group_by_model_alias=true`, `group_by_embed_dim=false`, `pad_to_largest_request=false`.

alex.h: that pad_to_largest_request=false is suspicious. If the batcher merged a 1024 and 1536 request without padding or validating, the runtime should have thrown earlier. logs?

jess.p: customer supplied a minimal repro. they send a mixed stream of 1-3 items per request during burst. attaching their request sample:```json
{"inputs": ["text A"], "model": "rdw-open-embed", "client_id": "acme-123"}
{"inputs": ["text B", "text C"], "model": "rdw-open-embed", "client_id": "acme-123"}
```

sam.k: can we get batcher debug trace for that time window? especially the batch composition records.

infra-bot: batcher-trace: [1723456700-1723456760] entries show: `batch_id=bn-9876: grouped alias=rdw-open-embed -> {variant: v1 (dim=1536), variant: v2 (dim=1024)}; emitted micro-batches: 4; final payloads: mixed-dims=true`. Also metrics show micro-batch wait increased from 8ms->40ms.

alex.h: root cause looks like alias resolution returned multiple variants and group_by_model_alias merged them. As our runtime dispatch assumes consistent embed dim per batch, that produced the dimension mismatch for payloads routed to the wrong kernel.

maria.t: short-term mitigation for customer: force single-request (no coalescing) by setting header `x-redwood-no-batch: 1` or set `max_batch_size=1` at their API key. That will avoid mixed batches immediately.

jess.p: sent customer the no-batch header suggestion and offered to toggle their project max_batch_size to 1 for an hour while we patch. they replied yes, wants quick fix.

sam.k: medium-term fix: change batcher grouping to consider resolved embed_dim (or model fingerprint) rather than alias only. Also enable pad_to_largest_request=true as a safety if dims match via padding rules for token embeddings, but for embedding dim different we must never coalesce. Add assertion to batcher that all resolved variants in a batch have identical embed_dim.

alex.h: agree. will open a hotfix PR to add embed_dim grouping and a defensive assert. Also add an integration test that simulates alias mapping returning mixed-dim variants.

sam.k: PR gist:```diff
- group_key = (alias)
+ group_key = (alias, resolved_model.embed_dim)
+ assert all(v.embed_dim == resolved_model.embed_dim for v in group_variants), "mixed embed_dim in batch"
```

maria.t: also schedule a rolling restart of batcher instances after deploy to ensure new grouping is picked up; we'll monitor 95th latency and embed error rate.

jess.p: customer confirmed short-term toggle worked — error rate dropped to 0 and 95th latency back to normal. thanked us.

infra-bot: Monitoring: post-toggle window [1723456780-1723456800]: embed_dim_mismatch errors -> 0, 95p latency -> 130ms.

alex.h: timeline/owners: sam -> hotfix PR + unit tests (2h). infra -> rolling restart post-merge (ops ticket). support -> keep customer updated and revert max_batch_size back after patch.

jess.p: filing support follow-up with repro steps so customer can test after deploy. Also asked if we should backport to the last stable branch since alias change landed recently.

sam.k: yes backport to release-1.8.1. i'll include a changelog note.

jess.p: closing loop with customer now. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
